recipes.name: Slow Cooker Sweet and Sour Meatballs
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle chile sauce

steps.text: Whisk together chile sauce, grape jelly, and lemon juice. Pour into a slow cooker and simmer over Low heat until warm.
Combine ground beef, onion, egg, and salt. Mix well and form into 24 1-inch balls. Add to sauce and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Sweet and Sour Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for sweet and sour meatballs is easy to prepare in the slow cooker and gets extra flavor from a delicious sauce with a secret ingredient.

review.reviewBody: Okay, I cheated. I used a box of frozen fully cooked meatballs. However, that sauce is to die for! A really nice change from our standard sweet&sour bottled sauce. I put the frozen meatballs and sauce in the slow cooker on low and they were ready 4 hours later. A double thumbs up from this family.

I have never cooked homemade meatballs. I cooked them for dinner and they were sooooo good that I had to tell my son who DOES NOT like meatballs to save some for others and my mother who said they'd be nasty with ground turkey, asking me to cook more the next day. Due to my inability to find the proper sauce and reading other helpful reviews about precooking the meatballs first, I tweaked my recipe a little. For the meatballs I used 3lbs of ground turkey, 1 grated onion and 2 large eggs. I baked them in the oven on 350 degrees until browned on both sides. For the sauce I used one 12oz bottle of House Of Tsang - Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce (from Target...so frigging good) and poured it over the meatballs and let everything cook until the sauce boiled. (NOTE: This sauce does not need to be mixed with lemon and/or jelly. Although I bought grape jelly I did not need to doctor the sauce as it already has a delicious sweet/spicy taste) I served them with homemade mash potatoes and a mixture of sweet cream corn and fire roasted whole corn. There was no trace of food once plates were fixed. lol This will definitely be going in my recipe book that I'm building.

Great recipe, but recipe should include the following information: Cook your meatballs in the oven first before adding to your sauce and use the Heinz chili sauce. I bought Asian garlic chili sauce at first. Luckily I tested a small sample and figured out I had the wrong chili sauce. Finally, the meatballs need to cook for about 3 hours in the sauce so that the flavor will be absorbed into the meatballs. The end result was excellent!

These were a hit at a Cotton Bowl party for the Fightin' Texas Aggies! The recipe is super easy. I doubled the recipe for a larger group. The meatballs took only a few minutes to roll, and I was able to use grass-fed beef. I also baked them in the oven for 60 minutes at 350 degrees and then finished them off in a crock pot at the party. These are now my favorite appetizers to take parties.

I have been wanting to make this for a really long time! The grape jelly/ chili sauce combo is posted almost everywhere anytime you search for slowcooker meatball recipes. I liked the addition of lemon in this one. I added the juice of half a lemon, and minced 2 cloves of garlic to the sauce as well. Also made my own meatball recipe, which i just had to cook quickly for a bit in the oven to brown and drain some fat. I do highly suggest that these are browned and fat drained first. ..but that's a personal preference. I overall loved this dish, and i am not a huge meatball fan.

I didn't use the slow cooker, just put everything in my braising pot for a couple of hours on low, added pineapple chunks and used frozen meatballs. It was okay. I think I prefer homemade meatballs but for convenience, you can't beat the frozen. Hubby really liked this and we both heated up leftovers the next day for our lunches which went well so will be repeating this one. Pretty good.

I've made this twice....both times I used 93% lean ground turkey instead of beef. The second time I halved the onion amount which helped keep the meatballs together(also if you heat up the sauce in the slow cooker on high and then reduce it to low once you put the meatballs in, it hels keep them from falling apart). YUM YUM YUM!!!!....great served over egg fried quinoa :)

This recipe was really, really good,even my picky teenager liked it. After cooking the meatballs, I removed them from the pan, drained most of the drippings then sautéed onions, snow peas & celery (what I had on hand; was wishing I had water chestnuts too) until tender, then returned the meatballs to the pan and added the sauce. Outstanding!

I almost always try a recipe as is before I alter it to my taste, however I couldn't wait to try this one so I used what I had on hand. First, I used ground turkey instead of beef, second I used apricot pineapple preserves instead of grape jelly. I did decide last minute to brown the meatballs in a skillet before putting them in the slow cooker. The balls, which I formed using a cookie scoop, didn't seem too sturdy and I wasn't convinced that they wouldn't fall apart. They simmered for an hour and a half and the sauce still seemed kind of watery so I cranked it up to high with the lid off so it could reduce some for about 30 to 45 more minutes. They were really yummy. My hubby rated it a 9 out of 10 and insisted that he take some to his buddy. I only got one :o(. I will surely make this again, next time I'll try it as is.

I’ve been making these party meatballs for years but much simpler — Frozen meatballs, chili sauce, grape jam. 
I found the flavors don’t soak into the meatballs as well if you only use the crockpot. So, do them in a stockpot on the stove the night before, in the fridge overnight, crockpot the day of the party for hot meatballs!
Made this and it was awesome! Made my own meatballs. Basically the same as in this recipe,but added breadcrumbs and browned them before putting in the crock pot. Everyone loved them.

This was really good. The sauce is excellent. I did make a couple of adjustments. I added some bread crumbs to the meat. I was concerned that the meatballs cooking in the liquid will not stay solid. No problems. The crock pot of course makes more liquid while cooking which diluted that great sauce. To fix this I thickened the liquid and it was great. Very tasty. I will make again. Thanks for the recipe.

I love this sauce, I had been making it for years with ribs in the slow cooker. Chilli ketchup works excellent instead of actual chilli sauce. It’s easy and fast to make on a busy night or when you’re not so keen on cooking for hours after a long day. I highly recommend this and you will not be disappointed. 😊 Also, if I don’t have grape jelly, I use apricot jelly, or any fruit jelly I have around. Still excellent!
I made this, and it turned out so Hot (spicy) . I used Thailand chile sauce. I think it would be a 5 star if it didn't burn my insides!!
Couldn't get grape jelly. So used strawberry jelly instead. They came out fine. Used IKEA swedish meatballs instead of making my own. Also good.

I have to start by saying that I HATE sweet and sour sauce. However, my husband and three kids LOVE it. Seriously, they eat it with everything. So when I saw this recipe I figured I would give it a shot. I, myself, tried it and, of course, didn’t care for it. So technically this review is coming from my husband and boys and they absolutely ADORED it! They said it was the best sweet and sour sauce they had ever tried and definitely want me to make the dish again. I did make double the recipe and it was gone in a ridiculously short amount of time. They loved the sauce so much that they requested I make just the sauce for them to dip with other things. Whether or not I eat it, anything that can make my family this happy definitely calls for a five star review. Thanks so much for a simple amazing recipe. Btw, I used the Heinz chili sauce and great value versions of the lemon juice and grape jelly.
GREAT!!!

This was a hit at a potluck. I was hosting and a dozen people and made 3 dozen chicken on a sticks and 3 dozen of these meatballs ( sorry I used frozen). The chicken on the sticks were slow to go but the meatballs were out in no time. I used the 12 oz chili sauce, 6 oz of grape jelly and a couple of squirts of dijon mustard. so so good! i could have made 3 more dozens and they would have went.

Great Recipe. I used Kroger's Chili Sauce to make my recipe. It was super quick to make and easy to prepare. I won't admit it. But, I cheated. I used frozen meatballs. I would say that they have a different texture that homemade meatballs. So, next time I will make them from scratch. Also, I had some leftovers. so I put small amounts of them in ziplock sandwich bags. Then put in freezer bag. So I can reheat them (later) for snacks when the kids are hungry or after school.
very sweet.
